clue.text: Drug, say, abused by weird sect

indicators.note: by places the jumbled sect beside the jumbled say, the sect part coming first
weird says the letters of sect are twisted into a strange new order
abused says the letters of say are mistreated and knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A drug is misused by members of an odd religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals each work on one word: 'weird' turns SECT into ECST and 'abused' turns SAY into ASY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is the street name for the recreational drug MDMA.

clue.text: A number of West Indians in clubs play so badly

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: badly says the letters of play so are put out of order

explanation.surface: Caribbean musicians perform poorly at nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song, not a figure; 'badly' rearranges PLAY SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a type of song from the Caribbean, so a musical number.

clue.text: Experience discrimination, in a sense

definitions.meaning: to experience something briefly, as in having a ... of freedom
discrimination in the sense of good judgement in matters of style
one of the five senses, along with sight and smell

explanation.surface: Someone experiences unfair treatment, in some sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste can mean to experience, refined judgement, and the sense of flavour.

clue.text: Scholar dipped into Sanskrit works in Asian island

indicators.note: dipped into means the scholar goes inside the Sanskrit word

parts.note: a sutra is a Sanskrit text of aphorisms
MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar

explanation.surface: An academic browses Sanskrit texts on an Asian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large island in Indonesia, in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Comply about order to boxer showing weight problem

indicators.note: about means the word for comply wraps round the command

parts.note: to comply with a rule is to obey it
a boxer is a breed of dog, and sit is a command given to a dog

explanation.surface: A boxer told to follow orders is found to be overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter, but here it is the dog breed, so the order is SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity is the medical condition of being seriously overweight.

clue.text: Air transport for pompous officers

definitions.meaning: after Colonel Blimp, a cartoon figure of a reactionary British officer

explanation.definitionFit: Blimps are small airships and also blustering old-fashioned officers named after a cartoon colonel.

clue.text: Reconstructed in stages our prehistoric specimen

indicators.note: reconstructed means the letters of stages our are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A museum reassembles a fossil creature in stages.
explanation.definitionFit: A stegosaur is a plated dinosaur, a prehistoric animal.

clue.text: Spy it in damaged tree?

indicators.note: in means the two pieces sit inside the jumbled tree
damaged says the letters of tree are knocked out of shape

parts.note: M, the head of the secret service in the Bond stories, stands for a spy

explanation.surface: Look for the pest responsible inside a damaged tree.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the Bond spymaster, standing loosely for a spy; read as a whole, the clue tells you where to look for the insect, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are wood-eating insects found in damaged trees.

clue.text: 14, 16 and 17; or 3 and 25; or 1, 13 and 22

parts.note: the first group are anagrams of US states (Minnesota, Texas, Maine); the second are anagrams of each other; the third are mental conditions

explanation.walkthrough: Three readings: 14, 16 and 17 rearrange MINNESOTA, TEXAS and MAINE; 3 and 25 are rearrangements of each other; 1, 13 and 22 are changed mental conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: An altered state is a changed condition of mind, and anagrammed states are literally altered states.

clue.text: Applauds at regular intervals? That's a positive sign

indicators.note: at regular intervals says to take every second letter of applauds

explanation.surface: Clapping at steady intervals is a sign of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The plus symbol is called the positive sign in arithmetic.

clue.text: Centre of common extended a short distance

definitions.text: Centre of common extended a short distance

parts.words: Centre of common extended a short distance
parts.note: the middle letters of common are MM, the abbreviation for a small unit of length; written out in full, that abbreviation is the answer

explanation.surface: The middle of a village green has been stretched a little way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' looks like a village green, but only its middle two letters matter; 'extended' means write the abbreviation out as a full word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth of a metre is a very small distance, and mm is its standard abbreviation.

clue.text: Attend at university, initially optimistic

indicators.note: initially says the university word goes first, before the words for attend

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
to attend an event is to be at it

explanation.surface: Going to university makes someone hopeful at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attend' is split into the two words BE AT; 'initially' puts UP before them.
explanation.definitionFit: An upbeat person is cheerful and hopeful about the future.

clue.text: Intense happiness rising in English house, with strain receding

parts.note: rising means going up

indicators.note: receding means the word for strain goes backwards

parts.note: a strain is a tune or air

explanation.surface: Feelings rise in an English home as music fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress, but it is a tune; HO is a standard abbreviation for house, as in property listings.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is a feeling of intense excitement and joy.

clue.text: Puts up at home, having no friends around

indicators.note: around means the phrase for friendless is placed round the word for at home

parts.note: no mates is British slang for someone friendless
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A lonely person puts guests up at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts up' looks like giving a guest a bed, but means proposing a candidate. NO MATES (British slang for friendless) wraps IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up for a post is to propose them as a candidate.

clue.text: Part of design I tabled that's not fireproof

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A plan was put forward for something that could catch fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be set alight is by nature not proof against fire.

clue.text: A certain thing Tory leader cuts

definitions.note: singular in the clue: the saying counts death and taxes as the two certain things in life

indicators.note: leader says to take the first letter of Tory

parts.note: axes as a verb means cuts, as in cutting jobs or budgets

explanation.surface: A Conservative party leader slashes spending.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying that nothing is certain except death and taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names taxes, with death, as one of life's only certainties.

clue.text: A source of mineral or organic compound

parts.note: minerals are dug from a mine

explanation.surface: A clue about where minerals or organic compounds come from.
explanation.definitionFit: An amine is a chemical compound derived from ammonia, a class of organic substances.

clue.text: Fabulous creature many admire at sea

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, so many

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of admire are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors admire a legendary being out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives M; 'at sea' rearranges ADMIRE into ERMAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A mermaid is a mythical sea creature, fabulous meaning from fable.

clue.text: A secret I wrongly revealed about old arcane stuff

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for old
wrongly says the letters of a secret I are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to having wrongly given away an old secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges A SECRET I into ESTERICA, which goes round O; 'revealed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure matters understood only by a select few.

clue.text: Place in Africa is one surrounded by fish

indicators.note: surrounded by means the inner letters are enclosed by the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A place in Africa where a lone person is encircled by fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Company's board relocated in European city

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: relocated says the letters of board are moved about

explanation.surface: A firm's directors move to a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordoba is a city in Andalusia in southern Spain.

clue.text: In which one's not aware there's new suspicion going round

indicators.note: going round means the word for suspicion wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: a trace or suspicion means a slight hint

explanation.surface: Someone unaware that new suspicion is circulating.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a half-conscious state in which a person is unaware of surroundings.

clue.text: Conservative ceremony to publicise backing for standards

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: backing means the word for publicise is read in reverse

parts.note: to air an opinion is to make it public

explanation.surface: A Conservative event is staged to promote support for party principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards by which something is judged.

clue.text: Type in scientific journal

definitions.meaning: a type or character, as in 'it is not in his ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Nature means basic kind or character, and is also the title of a famous science journal.

clue.text: It's hard for a seed to finish important match with ace

indicators.note: to finish says the ace comes at the end, after the match

parts.note: a Test match is an important international cricket game
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A tennis seed finds it hard to close out a big match with an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match. 'seed' sounds like tennis, but is a plant seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The testa is the hard outer coat of a seed.

clue.text: Indications of a lot of hard drinkers going on spree

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word hard, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: bingers are people who drink heavily in bouts

explanation.surface: Lots of heavy drinkers heading out on a spree are signs of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims the final D from HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Harbingers are signs or forerunners of something to come.

clue.text: Pack to put between opposing card players

indicators.note: put between means the small word goes inside the pair of players

parts.note: in bridge, South and West sit on opposing sides

explanation.surface: Players face each other across a card table with a pack.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play against East-West, so S and W are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to pack it away.

clue.text: Put together around this spot, firmly fixed

indicators.note: around means the word for put together wraps round the word for this spot

parts.note: to add numbers is to put them together
here means this spot

explanation.surface: Something is assembled on the spot and fixed firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that adhered stuck fast to a surface.

clue.text: A vehicle endlessly hemmed in by others in capital

indicators.note: hemmed in by means the inner letters are surrounded by the word for others

parts.note: the others are further vehicles, that is, cars

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for vehicle loses its last letter

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car is stuck in traffic surrounded by others in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CAR to CA; 'others' means other vehicles, CARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital city of Venezuela.
